correctness.rationale: The lower bound follows exactly from maximum disjoint 1-/2-coordinate recovery capacity of each of seven binary nonzero request types, summation to 4n minus half the discrepancy, and integer balancing. At n=11 and n=12 the necessary total capacities are 38<42 and 43<49 respectively; padding rules out shorter lengths. Actual certificate contents provide valid pairwise-disjoint XOR recovery subsets for every one of 924 six-request and 1716 seven-request multisets, for full-rank generators of lengths 12 and 13. Standalone replay verified all inputs and computations.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial rank-three binary two-locality functional batch design has a natural optimization question for each simultaneous-request count. These exact adjacent six-/seven-request optima close a precise finite resource/storage tradeoff relevant to the current restricted-recovery literature. The distinction between equal-request necessary capacity and simultaneous mixed-request sufficiency is addressed by verifiable complete certificates, so the finding is more than a simple parameter substitution or untested numeric claim.
